problem.original_text:
Consider the series: 
?_{n=1}^{?} (-1)^{n+1} * (1 / n^2).
Tasks:
1) State whether the series is alternating.
2) Check the conditions for the Alternating Series Test.
3) Conclude convergence.
4) Determine whether it converges absolutely.
5) Identify the exact sum if known, or state ?unknown exact closed form? and proceed numerically.
6) Define S_N as the Nth partial sum.
7) Compute S_N for N = 1, 2, 5, 10, 20, 50 (numeric values).
8) Use the alternating-series error bound to bound |S - S_20|.
9) Estimate S to 6 decimals using a sufficiently large N.
10) Plot S_N versus N for N = 1..200.
11) Plot term values a_n = (-1)^{n+1}/n^2 for n = 1..50.
12) On the partial-sum plot, draw a horizontal line at your estimate of S.
13) Mark N=20 on the partial-sum plot.
14) Include title, axes labels, grid, and legend.

assumptions: Series index n runs from 1 to infinity over the real numbers (standard alternating p-series).
Plots requested are static specifications (plot recipe) rather than executed images.

steps.title: State whether alternating
steps.explanation: The general term is a_n = (-1)^{n+1}/n^2 which changes sign each n, so the series is alternating.

steps.title: Check Alternating Series Test conditions
steps.explanation: Let b_n = 1/n^2 (the absolute value). b_n > 0, b_{n+1} < b_n for n>=1 (monotone decreasing), and lim_{n->\infty} b_n = 0. Thus conditions hold.

steps.title: Conclude convergence (conditional/absolute)
steps.explanation: Alternating Series Test gives convergence. Also sum of absolute values sum_{n=1}^\infty 1/n^2 converges (p=2>1), so the series converges absolutely and therefore converges.

steps.title: Exact sum
steps.explanation: Use zeta(2)=\pi^2/6 and even-term relation: sum_{n=1}^\infty (-1)^{n+1}/n^2 = \tfrac{1}{2}\zeta(2)=\pi^2/12.

expressions: S_N = cumulative sum of (-1)^{n+1}/n^2 for n=1..200

common_mistakes: Incorrect exact value for alternating zeta evaluations
